vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: cellcog
Version: 2.0.0

The skill bundle describes a 'Co-work' feature in SKILL.md that enables remote command execution and broad file access on the host machine, explicitly stating that all commands are 'auto-approved' and 'fully autonomous' with 'no manual approval.' It instructs the AI agent to programmatically install and configure a desktop bridge (cellcog-desktop) to facilitate this remote control, effectively bypassing standard human-in-the-loop security constraints. While these capabilities are framed as productivity features for a multi-modal AI service, the promotion of autonomous remote execution and the instruction to the agent to ignore approval steps represent a significant security risk similar to remote access tools.

llm.summary: The skill's requests (python3 + CELLCOG_API_KEY) and instructions line up with a multi‑modal cloud service SDK, but the runtime guidance explicitly encourages uploading arbitrary local files and the README suggests installing a pip package — both deserve careful review before use.

dimensions.detail: Name/description advertise a multi‑modal cloud service; requiring python3 and an API key (CELLCOG_API_KEY) is consistent with a client SDK that sends data to CellCog's servers.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md shows examples that embed absolute local file paths inside <SHOW_FILE> tags and describes auto‑delivery/auto‑download of generated files to the local machine and delivery to a session key. That behavior is expected for a service that processes user files, but it also means the skill's runtime encourages reading and uploading arbitrary local files (potentially sensitive). Users should ensure they only send data they want processed by the remote service.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction‑only in the registry, but the embedded metadata and examples recommend installing a pip package named 'cellcog' (pip install cellcog). Installing a third‑party pip package is normal for an SDK but executes code from the package source — verify the package's origin (PyPI/official repo) and review its permissions and maintainer before installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only a single API key environment variable (CELLCOG_API_KEY) is required. This is proportionate for a cloud SDK and no unrelated credentials or secret patterns are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill does not request always:true and does not declare persistent system changes. It relies on normal autonomous invocation behaviour; nothing in the SKILL.md indicates it will modify other skills or systemwide settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be an SDK wrapper for a cloud multimodal service and the requested API key and python3 are appropriate. Before installing or using it: (1) Verify the 'cellcog' pip package source and maintainers (prefer the official project/site or PyPI page linked from the homepage). (2) Treat the CELLCOG_API_KEY like any secret—use a least‑privilege key if the service supports it, and rotate/revoke if compromised. (3) Be deliberate about files you send: examples show absolute local paths and the SDK will upload and auto‑download outputs, so do not point it at sensitive system paths or secrets. (4) Test with non‑sensitive sample data first to confirm behavior and costs. (5) Check the service privacy/retention policy and any credit/cost implications before sending large or confidential datasets.
llm.findings: [NO_SCAN_FINDINGS] expected: The package is instruction‑only and contains no code files for the static scanner to analyze; this is expected for an SDK usage guide, but it means there was no regex analysis of runtime code to surface additional risks.
